latest_release.body:
- New Homescreen, favorites under the card on 16:9 units, and drawer tabs for shortcuts, thanks to @andrecuellar
- Home: a separate switch for the widgets, and a panel opacity slider
- Settings: redesign the screen in Material 3 and make the accent blue, thanks to @andrecuellar
- Settings: a help button on every setting, sections ordered by use, a rail that folds to its icons, and one Bluetooth choice for Native AA
- Settings: remove the Fake Speed switch that did nothing, thanks to @teodortomas
- Wizard: test the decoder before recommending settings, thanks to @andrecuellar
- Status pill: stop saying Android Auto is starting when nothing is, thanks to @andrecuellar
- Added: Night overlay and gesture settings, with ILL+ calibration for the car_mode signal, thanks to @Anton111111
- Gestures: keep two-finger gestures off Android Auto, add edge taps, a two-finger swipe down, a dimmer and more overlay settings, thanks to @o-jcardenass and @Anton111111
- Added: Device-specific settings for Adayo (Haval) head units, thanks to @Anton111111
- Added: Scaling for the exit dialog, thanks to @Anton111111
- Automation: end the session when the charger is removed, turn the screen off and on, and connect a phone by name or MAC
- Overlay: show the head unit's battery, free memory and WiFi signal
- Native AA: connect faster
- Added: Bluetooth relay (ESP32) for Native AA, thanks to @kendrickkim
- Native AA: carry the handshake over the ZJ Bluetooth socket on Unisoc units, thanks to @justme-justus
- Native AA: support confirmed HCT Bluetooth bridges without root, thanks to @emotionbug
- WiFi Direct: detect a wedged P2P stack and offer a WiFi restart, and remember a unit that refuses every banded group, thanks to @mark-alexander-hub
- WiFi: Pause automatic searches during wireless sessions with Shizuku, thanks to @emotionbug
- Wireless: keep owned WPP channels across a projection Exit, and fix legacy Wi-Fi Direct metadata and cleanup callbacks, thanks to @emotionbug
- Hotspot: start tethering once, so auto-enable no longer tears down its own access point, thanks to @Duzttt
- Bluetooth auto-disconnect: end the session when the phone closes the held channel, thanks to @mohammed-just
- Bluetooth: open the app on units without a Bluetooth manager, and check ZBT reachability without activating the module, thanks to @emotionbug
- Bluetooth: apply XYAuto media policy automatically during wireless projection, thanks to @emotionbug
- USB: stop the permission dialog that comes back on every connect, let a plug-in leave the phone alone, and recover a lost link
- Fix(usb): Resolve dongle AOA switching
- AAP: send one version request over TCP, so a slow head unit server is not left deaf
- AAP: Keep media and navigation display updates off the receive path, and preserve frame boundaries during handshake, thanks to @emotionbug
- Video: Add H.264 support to bundled FFmpeg, reduce decoder polling and preserve recovery ownership, thanks to @emotionbug
- Projection: keep the decoder through a short cover, thanks to @andrecuellar
- Projection: fill the screen with a SurfaceView below Android 7
- Display: size Automatic DPI to the panel, and keep the widescreen layout it already had
- UI: respect system insets and refresh forced-scale projection geometry, thanks to @emotionbug
- Audio: Reduce renderer work, add independent music correction, and keep microphone foreground ownership across service starts, thanks to @emotionbug
- Audio: tap a channel's percentage to type an exact value, and raise the amplification ceiling to 250%, thanks to @teodortomas
- Android 4.x: keep GPS location resends and Self-ADB working on older versions, thanks to @emotionbug
- Fix: crash on ROMs that lack Activity.isDestroyed, and in the WiFi restart switch and the OEM app dialog on Android 4.2
- Updates: offer only a release whose APK is uploaded
- Translations: rewrite every locale against Android's own translations, and add the Wi-Fi scan screen, the

detail.readme:
# Open Headunit

Open Headunit is an Android app that allows you to turn your Android tablet or phone into an Android Auto receiver. This project is a revived version of the original headunit project by the great Michael Reid. The original project can be found here: https://github.com/mikereidis/headunit It runs on Android 4.1 and newer (Android 5.0 and newer for the Play Store build). Besides the stores above, you can download APKs from the [Releases page](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/releases). **Contents:** [How to use](#how-to-use) · [Known Issues](#known-issues) · [Planned](#planned) · [Changelog](#changelog) · [Contributing](#contributing) ## NOTE! **Android Auto 17.4 and newer can prevent legacy wireless triggers from launching projection, including Self-Mode and automated startup via Wireless Helper. Rooted devices have a workaround: re-enable Android Auto's wireless startup receiver.** Use a **USB wireless dongle**, **Native Mode** or the **Headunit Server** instead. **Wireless Helper** works up to Android Auto **17.3**, or on **17.4+** with the root workaround. See [Wireless Connection Options](#wireless-connection-options). ## Screenshots ## How to use **Check out the [Wiki](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki) for detailed documentation, setup guides and troubleshooting!** ### Wired USB Connection - Connect your Android device (phone) to the tablet running Open Headunit via USB cable. - Make sure that Android Auto is installed on your phone. - Set your phone to Host-Mode if necessary and select Android Auto - Click the USB Button in Open Headunit, find your phone and click the right button to allow connection - Click on your phone in the list and wait for Android Auto to start Once a phone is set up, plugging it in connects by itself. You can change this in the Auto-start settings with **Connect when plugged in**. ### Wireless Connection Options Choose from the five options below depending on your Android Auto version and setup: #### 1. USB Wireless Android Auto Dongle (Most Reliable) - A standard hardware USB Wireless Android Auto Dongle (plugged into the headunit) handles the entire wireless negotiation independently. - Provides seamless plug-and-play connection regardless of phone Android Auto version. #### 2. Native Mode (Wi-Fi Direct / Headunit Hotspot) - Directly communicates with Android Auto's native wireless protocol without helper apps. - Supports **Wi-Fi Direct (P2P)** or the **Headunit Hotspot** transport. - Configure under Open Headunit Settings -> **Wireless Connection** -> **Wireless Mode** -> **Native**. - Native Mode starts over Bluetooth, then moves to WiFi. **Detect automatically** fits most units. Units that keep Bluetooth on a separate module, or that use a relay, take one of these routes: - **[ZLink module](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#zlink-bluetooth-module-experimental) (experimental):** units with a ZJ/ZLink Bluetooth service on port 3152. - **[ZJ socket](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#zj-bluetooth-socket):** Unisoc units whose module uses `/dev/socket/zj_bt_socket`. - **[FYT BLINK module](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#fyt-external-bluetooth-module-transport-experimental) (experimental):** FYT units with a separate module, such as DUDUAUTO on DUDUOS. - **[HCT service](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#hct-bluetooth-service):** units with a verified HCT Bluetooth service, without root. The app detects it by itself. - **[ESP32 relay](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#bluetooth-relay-esp32-classic-bt-relay):** an original ESP32 relays the handshake. Firmware: [aa-native-bt-broker-for-openheadunit](https://github.com/kendrickkim/aa-native-bt-broker-for-openheadunit). #### 3. Headunit Server (No-Root Option for Self-Mode on AA 17.4+) - Starts the native Android Auto developer server directly on your phone or on the same device (Self-Mode). - **Setup:** 1. Open Android Auto settings on your phone (or tablet in Self-Mode). 2. Scroll down and tap **Version** 10 times to unlock Developer settings. 3. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner and choose **Start headunit server**. 4. In Open Headunit, tap the **WiFi** button to connect (or use Self-Mode). #### 4. Wireless Helper - Our companion app triggers the wireless connection automatically in the background. - **Compatibility:** Android Auto **v17.3 and below**, or **v17.4+** with the root workaround in option 5. - **Download:** [Wireless Helper on Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.andrerinas.wirelesshelper) - **Setup:** Set Open Headunit **Wireless Mode** to **Wireless Helper**, ensure both devices are in the same network or Wi-Fi Direct group, and start the service in the Wireless Helper app. #### 5. Root Workaround for Android Auto 17.4+ On a rooted device running Android Auto, one shell command restores the previous wireless startup flow, so Wireless Helper keeps working. See the [command and its limits](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#5-root-workaround-for-android-auto-174). ### Optional automatic Wi-Fi scan pause This is a setting, not a way to connect. On Android 8 and newer, Open Headunit can pause Android's automatic Wi-Fi searches during a Native wireless connection, through Shizuku. It is off by default. See the [setup and limits per Android version](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Wireless#optional-automatic-wi-fi-scan-pause). ### Connect Wirelessly via Intent (Power Users) You can trigger a wireless connection attempt using an Android Intent. This is useful for automation tools like **Tasker**, **MacroDroid**, or via **ADB**. **URI Scheme:** `headunit://connect?ip=` **Example ADB Command:** ```bash adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "headunit://connect?ip=192.168.1.25" ``` The [Automation guide](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Automation) lists every command. ## Known Issues - **Google Maps in Portrait Mode:** Touch interactions (searching, scrolling) within Google Maps may not work as expected when using Portrait Mode on some devices. **Fix:** Try reducing the **Pixel density (DPI)** setting to **below 200** (e.g., 190) in the app settings. This often restores full functionality. - **Wireless Connection Drops:** If the connection drops frequently, disable **"WiFi Assistant"** or **"Switch between networks"** in your phone's WiFi settings to prevent it from killing the connection due to "no internet." Check battery saving options. - **Self-mode on Android 10 (Q) and below:** Google has disabled the automatic wireless projection startup for Android 10 and below in Android Auto versions 16.4 and higher. While Self-mode still works on newer Android versions, it is normally impossible to trigger projection on Android 10 and below directly with recent Google app updates. **Workaround:** You can still use Self-mode on these devices by starting the built-in Android Auto Headunit Server and connecting via Wi-Fi mode (loopback). See the [Troubleshooting Guide](https://github.com/andreknieriem/open-headunit/wiki/Troubleshooting#self-mode-on-android-10-q-and-below) for step-by-step instructions. - **WiFi Direct takes a long time to connect:** One user traced this to Google Assistant in Android Auto. With Gemini on newer Android Auto versions it runs smoothly again. We do not know why. - **Stuck on "Android Auto is starting":** Check your video codec in the settings, and set it to H.264 if your device does not support H.265. Some devices have a broken H.265 decoder, which leaves the app stuck on this message. ## Planned - more customization options for the UI and the app itself ## Changelog ### 4.0.0 - New Homescreen, favorites under the card on 16:9 units, and drawer tabs for shortcuts, thanks to @andrecuellar - Overlay: show the head unit's battery, free memory and WiFi signal - Native AA: connect faster - Added: Bluetooth relay (ESP32) for Native AA, thanks to @kendrickkim - Native AA: carry the handshake over the ZJ Bluetooth socket on Unisoc units, thanks to @justme-justus - Create one in the root folder: ```bash keytool -genkey -v -keystore headunit-release-key.jks -alias headunit-revived -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 ``` Then set the passwords as environment variables, for example in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`: ```bash export HEADUNIT_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD="YOUR_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" export HEADUNIT_KEY_PASSWORD="YOUR_KEY_PASSWORD" ``` ## Original Headunit Headunit for Android Auto (tm) A new car or a $600+ headunit is NOT required to enjoy the integration and distraction reduced environment of Android Auto.
